title: Ezekiel's Call to Be a Prophet

questions.question: What did the voice of the one speaking say to Ezekiel when he had fallen on his face?
options: "Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you."
"O mortal, hear my words and live."
"Servant of the Lord, look upon me."
questions.correctAnswer: "Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 2:1 (ESV): "And he said to me, 'Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you.'"

questions.question: What happened to Ezekiel as God spoke to him?
options: The Spirit entered into him and set him on his feet
A great wind lifted him into the air
Fire touched his lips and purified him
An angel took him by the hand
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit entered into him and set him on his feet
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 2:2 (ESV): "And as he spoke to me, the Spirit entered into me and set me on my feet, and I heard him speaking to me."

questions.question: To whom did God say He was sending Ezekiel?
options: To the people of Israel, to nations of rebels, who have rebelled against me
To the king of Babylon and his princes
Only to the priests remaining in Jerusalem
To the entire world, both Jew and Gentile
questions.correctAnswer: To the people of Israel, to nations of rebels, who have rebelled against me
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 2:3 (ESV): "And he said to me, 'Son of man, I send you to the people of Israel, to nations of rebels, who have rebelled against me.'"

questions.question: How does God describe the descendants of Israel to whom He is sending Ezekiel?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 2:4 (ESV): "The descendants also are impudent and stubborn: I send you to them,"

questions.question: What phrase is Ezekiel told to declare to them?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 2:4 (ESV): "and you shall say to them, 'Thus says the Lord God.'"

questions.question: "And whether they hear or refuse to hear (for they are a... ), they will know that a prophet has been among them."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 2:5 (ESV): "And whether they hear or refuse to hear (for they are a rebellious house) they will know that a prophet has been among them."

questions.question: "And you, son of man, be not... of them, nor be... of their words,"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 2:6 (ESV): "And you, son of man, be not afraid of them, nor be afraid of their words,"

questions.question: What does God compare the people to, when telling Ezekiel not to fear their words?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 2:6 (ESV): "though briers and thorns are with you and you sit on scorpions. Be not afraid of their words, nor be dismayed at their looks, for they are a rebellious house."

questions.question: What is Ezekiel warned NOT to be, like the rebellious house?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 2:8 (ESV): "But you, son of man, hear what I say to you. Be not rebellious like that rebellious house;"

questions.question: What command does God give Ezekiel regarding what is given to him?
options: "Open your mouth and eat what I give you."
"Take this scroll and read it aloud."
"Write these words on a tablet of stone."
questions.correctAnswer: "Open your mouth and eat what I give you."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 2:8 (ESV): "open your mouth and eat what I give you."

questions.question: When Ezekiel looked, what was sent to him in a hand?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 2:9 (ESV): "And when I looked, behold, a hand was stretched out to me, and behold, a scroll of a book was in it."

questions.question: How was the scroll unrolled and written on?
options: It had writing on the front and on the back
It was sealed with seven seals
It had writing only on the inside
It was empty until he touched it
questions.correctAnswer: It had writing on the front and on the back
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 2:10 (ESV): "And he unrolled it before me. And it had writing on the front and on the back,"

questions.question: What kinds of things were written on the scroll?
options: Words of lamentation and mourning and woe
Laws and statutes of a new temple
Genealogies and histories of the kings
questions.correctAnswer: Words of lamentation and mourning and woe
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 2:10 (ESV): "and there were written on it words of lamentation and mourning and woe."

questions.question: What title does God repeatedly use for Ezekiel throughout this chapter (and the entire book)?
Why are the people of Israel not expected to listen to Ezekiel?
options: Because they are a rebellious house
Because they did not understand his language
Because the Babylonians forbade them to listen
questions.correctAnswer: Because they are a rebellious house
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 2:5, 7, 8 (ESV): "...for they are a rebellious house."

key_verse_text: "And you shall speak my words to them, whether they hear or refuse to hear, for they are a rebellious house."
